requirement_text.ISS-0332: REQ-077 bumped the DEFINITION_PROMOTED platform-event-type seed from schema_version 1 (review_id required non-null) to schema_version 2 (review_id nullable) in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, to support R10. This seed only applies to tenants provisioned from this point forward -- nothing re-runs replay_migrations/2 or re-registers the type for already-provisioned tenants. R10 against such a tenant commits the promotion transaction, then fails the event-append step on schema validation -- a committed write reported as failure (Severity 1). Needs a backfill routine iterating tenant_schemas and calling Letflow.EventStore.Registry.register_type/2 per tenant, no-op on already-higher-version collision.

source_text.diagnosis: Root cause: maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 is called only during replay_migrations/2 (provisioning time). When @platform_event_type_seed_attrs changes (v1->v2 for DEFINITION_PROMOTED), no mechanism updates already-provisioned tenants' event_type_registry. R10's append_promotion_event call (outside any transaction) calls validate_payload/3 which queries the highest registered schema_version -- still v1 for pre-existing tenants -- and fails on null review_id, producing HTTP 500 while the promotion DB write is already committed (Severity-1 broken-audit shape). Fix must: iterate tenant_schemas, call register_type/2 per tenant for DEFINITION_PROMOTED v2 attrs, treat {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version} as no-op (already at v2). CODE-DESIGNER should also review whether the structural commit-before-event issue warrants a structural fix (outer transaction or idempotent retry) within this ISS-0332 scope or a separate issue.

task.description:
Design the fix for ISS-0332. Produce a design artefact at lib/letflow/design/iss0332-definition-promoted-backfill.md. No implementation code.

The design must cover:

1. **Scope decision**: Is the fix ONLY the backfill routine, or does it also address the structural issue that promote_active_definition/5 commits the target definition write before calling the event appender? Assess: (a) would an outer transaction around both the DB write and the event append be feasible given EventStore.append/2's structure? (b) or is an idempotent re-run/retry the right shape? Document your decision and rationale. If the structural issue is out of scope for ISS-0332 (too large, needs its own requirement), say so explicitly and file a note for a follow-on ISS.

2. **Backfill mechanism**: Define the @spec, module, and function name for the backfill. Options include:
   a. A Mix task (e.g. mix letflow.backfill_event_type_versions) that iterates Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Registration records and calls Letflow.EventStore.Registry.register_type/2 per tenant for each event type that needs a version bump.
   b. A module function in Letflow.TenantProvisioning (or a new Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Backfill module) callable from iex/ops.
   Both a and b can coexist -- the Mix task wrapping the module function is the idiomatic pattern. Choose and justify.

3. **register_type/2 return value handling**: Document how the backfill handles each return from register_type/2:
   - {:ok, _} -> new registration succeeded
   - {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version} -> already at this exact version, treat as success
   - {:error, :schema_version_not_monotonic} -> already at a HIGHER version, treat as success
   - {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} -> tenant_schemas row exists but no Registration? Log and skip, or halt?
   - {:error, other} -> halt with error

4. **@spec for any new public functions** -- no implementation bodies.

5. **Acceptance criteria mapping**: Map each of ISS-0332's three acceptance criteria to what the design produces:
   - AC1: backfill updates pre-existing tenants
   - AC2: R10 against a pre-existing tenant succeeds end-to-end (does the design address this, or does it only create the backfill and assume it will be run?)
   - AC3: idempotent on already-v2 tenants

Design doc must be unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without making new design decisions.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/design/iss0332-definition-promoted-backfill.md exists and covers all five design points above
Scope decision on the structural commit-before-event issue is stated explicitly
Backfill mechanism module/function/@spec is stated -- no implementation code
All register_type/2 return value cases are handled in the design
Every ISS-0332 acceptance criterion is mapped to a concrete design element
No implementation code in the design doc
